cefr_entry_assessment.target_learners: CEFR-Referenced A1–A2 (learners who understand common English words, recognize basic instructions, give simple personal information, understand familiar questions, form short statements, and participate in simple exchanges with support).
cefr_entry_assessment.pre_a1_consideration: Students with very limited English comprehension may receive preparatory support covering alphabet recognition, essential vocabulary, basic listening, greetings, and common classroom instructions. We do not automatically classify every complete beginner as A1.

diagnostic_components.description: Learner introduces themselves using familiar personal information.
Checks understanding and response to simple daily questions (name, origin, occupation, daily routine, interests).
Short beginner-level audio clip with simple comprehension check.
Checks basic positive statements, negative sentences, and question forms.
Supported beginner dialogue with teacher or peer.
Observes whether key words, sounds, and word stress can be readily understood.
Identifies personal daily communication, college, workplace, or confidence goals.

cefr_entry_assessment.critical_disclaimer: The entry diagnostic is an internal Nova Skills instructional reference, not an official Cambridge English, British Council, or Council of Europe certificate.

pronunciation_philosophy.headline: Clarity and Intelligibility Over Accent Elimination
pronunciation_philosophy.approach: Pronunciation training focuses on understandable communication, accurate word stress, natural rhythm, sentence stress, and clear key sounds. We celebrate and respect Indian English and diverse global English varieties. Accent elimination is neither required nor pedagogically sound.
core_distinctions: Intelligibility: ensuring listeners easily understand your words and meaning
Word Stress: placing stress on correct syllables (e.g., PHO-to-graph vs pho-TOG-ra-phy)
Sentence Stress & Rhythm: emphasizing content words to establish English speech rhythm
Intonation: using pitch variations to indicate questions, statements, and polite requests
Respect: no scoring based on mimicking British or American accents

optional_ai_assisted_learning.heading: Practise With AI. Improve With Human Feedback.
optional_ai_assisted_learning.philosophy: Use accessible AI speaking tools for extra conversation, pronunciation and listening practice where available. Instructor feedback remains central to assessment and learning progress.

tools.name: ChatGPT Voice
tools.use_cases: Short English conversations, greeting practice, everyday role-play, repeating simple questions, explaining basic expressions, slower guided practice.
tools.prompt_example: Act as a friendly beginner English conversation partner. Ask me one simple A1-level question at a time about everyday life. Use short sentences. Allow me to answer before asking another question. Correct only important communication errors and give one simple improvement suggestion after my response.
tools.limitations: Voice mode availability and limits depend on plan, account, and device settings. Transcripts may contain recognition errors.

tools.name: ELSA Speak
tools.use_cases: Phonetic practice, sound distinction drills, sentence-level speaking, intonation awareness.
tools.limitations: Free tier features are sufficient; paid Pro is never mandatory. Acoustic models may have regional biases; human teacher review remains primary.

tools.name: Cambridge Speak & Improve
tools.use_cases: Automated practice questions, rehearsal, listening to own recordings.
tools.limitations: Cambridge research project, NOT an official Cambridge qualification exam. Uploading voice samples is optional.

mandatory_safety_rules: Instructor-led speaking and peer practice remain primary
Student privacy and consent are strictly respected

Students can complete the course with 100% success without using AI apps

recording_consent_and_privacy.purpose: Audio recordings are used exclusively for learner self-reflection, instructor feedback, and baseline-versus-final comparison.
recording_consent_and_privacy.consent_protocol: Recordings are strictly voluntary and consent-based. Educational purpose is explained in advance.
recording_consent_and_privacy.privacy_safeguard: No student audio or video is ever shared publicly, published to marketing platforms, or uploaded to third-party public AI models.
recording_consent_and_privacy.alternative_assessment: Learners who prefer not to record audio may complete live instructor-observed speaking assessments evaluated under the identical rubric.

portfolio.title: Beginner Spoken English Development Portfolio
portfolio.description: A comprehensive, practical speaking development portfolio demonstrating measurable oral progress from baseline entry to final assessment, featuring recorded introductions, three realistic conversational simulations, listening records, pronunciation worksheets, a spontaneous talk, and an individualized continuing-learning plan.

deliverables.name: Component 01: Baseline & Final Introductions Comparison
deliverables.description: Comparative evaluation of a 60–90 second personal introduction recorded in Week 1 versus Week 4, tracking sentence completion, vocabulary range, pausing, clarity, and teacher feedback.

deliverables.name: Component 02: Three Real-Life Conversation Simulations
deliverables.description: Assessed role-play simulations covering (A) Meeting & Introducing People, (B) Everyday Service Situation (retail, food, travel, directions), and (C) Study or Basic Workplace Interaction.

deliverables.name: Component 03: Listening & Comprehension Assessment
deliverables.description: Standardized beginner listening evaluation testing main idea extraction, key numerical/time detail identification, instruction following, and appropriate verbal responses.

deliverables.name: Component 04: Pronunciation & Clarity Improvement Record
deliverables.description: Documented progress tracking targeted vowel/consonant distinctions, multi-syllable word stress, content-word sentence stress, rhythm, and listener intelligibility.

deliverables.name: Component 05: Two-to-Three-Minute Spontaneous Speaking Task
deliverables.description: Live or consent-recorded unscripted monologue on a familiar topic (daily routine, hometown, college, or hobby) demonstrating independent idea sequencing and conversational recovery.

deliverables.name: Component 06: Personalized Continuing-Learning Plan
deliverables.description: Actionable roadmap outlining current strengths, high-priority grammar/vocabulary targets, ongoing pronunciation drills, a daily speaking routine, and clear progression into Professional Spoken English.

faq.question: What is Spoken English Foundations & Everyday Conversation?
faq.answer: It is a beginner-focused course that develops essential speaking, listening, pronunciation and everyday conversation skills.

faq.question: Is the course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed mainly for learners around CEFR A1–A2 who need structured speaking practice.

faq.question: What if I know almost no English?
faq.answer: A diagnostic assessment can identify whether preparatory support is needed before or during the beginner pathway.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Four weeks with 32 guided learning hours.

faq.question: What is the course fee?
faq.answer: ₹3,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.

faq.question: Will I learn grammar?
faq.answer: Yes. Essential grammar is taught through practical sentence building and conversation rather than as an advanced grammar-only course.

faq.question: Will I learn pronunciation?
faq.answer: Yes. The course includes common sound distinctions, word stress, sentence stress, intonation and speaking clarity.

faq.question: Will the course remove my Indian accent?
faq.answer: No. The goal is clear and understandable communication, not removing a learner's natural accent.

faq.question: Will I practise everyday conversations?
faq.answer: Yes. You will practise introductions, questions, requests, opinions and familiar daily situations.

faq.question: Are listening exercises included?
faq.answer: Yes. You will practise understanding short conversations, simple instructions and everyday spoken English.

faq.question: Will I practise telephone conversations?
faq.answer: Yes. Basic telephone exchanges and clarification strategies are included.

faq.question: Will I practise speaking with classmates?
faq.answer: Yes. Instructor-led and paired speaking activities form part of the learning method.

faq.question: Will I receive speaking feedback?
faq.answer: Yes. The curriculum includes structured feedback and individual pronunciation and communication improvement notes.

faq.question: Will I record my speaking?
faq.answer: The course uses baseline and final speaking evidence. Appropriate consent, privacy practices and approved alternative assessment arrangements apply.

faq.question: Will I complete a speaking portfolio?
faq.answer: Yes. The portfolio includes introductions, three conversation simulations, listening assessment, pronunciation improvement, spontaneous speaking and a continuing-learning plan.

faq.question: What is the spontaneous speaking task?
faq.answer: A familiar-topic speaking activity lasting approximately two to three minutes, with appropriate beginner-level preparation and support.

faq.question: Is ChatGPT Voice included?
faq.answer: ChatGPT Voice is an optional supplementary practice tool where available. Access and limits depend on account settings and plan.

faq.question: Is ELSA Speak required?
faq.answer: No. ELSA Speak may support optional pronunciation practice, but paid features are not mandatory.

faq.question: What is Cambridge Speak & Improve?
faq.answer: It is a Cambridge English speaking practice and research tool, not a formal Cambridge qualification exam.

faq.question: Will I receive an official CEFR certificate?
faq.answer: No. The course uses CEFR-referenced teaching and diagnostics. Its internal assessment is not an official CEFR proficiency examination.

faq.question: Will I become fluent in four weeks?
faq.answer: The course builds foundational skills and gives structured practice. Complete fluency depends on starting level, continued learning and practice.

faq.question: Is this the same as Professional Spoken English?
faq.answer: No. This is a shorter beginner entry course. The longer Professional Spoken English programme provides broader and deeper training.

faq.question: Can I join Professional Spoken English afterward?
faq.answer: Yes, subject to the longer programme's current entry requirements and your learning needs.

faq.question: Is this suitable for job seekers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help build basic everyday and workplace introduction skills, but it does not replace professional interview or business communication training.

faq.question: Do I need paid apps?
faq.answer:
No. Core learning relies on instructor-led practice and accessible materials. Paid AI or pronunciation subscriptions are optional.
